description: Groundwater picture for a Texas address or coordinate from public state well records (TWDB Groundwater Database and TWDB/TDLR Submitted Drillers Reports, cleaned and refreshed monthly): which TWDB major and minor aquifers lie under the point (outcrop or subsurface), the groundwater conservation district (or none, which means rule of capture), supply wells within the radius with depth bands, reported yields (low, median and 75th percentile, weighted by test method; pump tests count most, jetted and estimated least), the highest-yield wells with depth, screen, aquifer and test method, a per-aquifer summary (wells, median depth, 75th percentile yield, median TDS with the newest sample year, median water-level trend in ft/yr), and flags. The groundwater district's adopted rules (exempt-well limits, permits, spacing, production caps per acre, export rules, fees, metering) with rule numbers, pages and short quotes, where two independent extractions agreed; otherwise a link to the rules. Optional demand_mgd or demand_gpm returns how many wells at the local 75th percentile yield would meet it, and the acres of groundwater rights a per-acre district cap implies. Use when someone asks about water for a data center, cooling, a plant, irrigation or a well: how deep, how much, how salty, who regulates it. Driller yields are completion estimates, not long-term capacity; district permits decide what can be pumped. Free shows the aquifers, district and well counts; Pro adds yields, depths, quality, trends, district rules and the well list.

address.description: Texas street address, e.g. '1201 Main St, Houston, TX'. Use this or lat/lng.

demand_gpm.description: Water demand in gallons per minute (optional; demand_mgd wins if both).

demand_mgd.description: Water demand in million gallons per day (optional).

lat.description: Latitude (WGS84). Use with lng instead of address.

lng.description: Longitude (WGS84). Use with lat instead of address.

radius_mi.description: Search radius in miles. Default 5, max 15.
